title: Why New Orleans clarinetists had individual sounds
summary: Barry asks why old New Orleans players had individuality while modern ones copy George Lewis; Joe says he never copied anyone.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: You say that there was nobody who really influenced you to that great...no one single person. It seems to me like all of the New Orleans clarinet players you hear, any of them, just name any name, they all sound like themselves -- individuals.

Now, if you take any European guy or any young guy or any of this, ten thousand of them copied George Lewis, ten thousand copied Barney, ten thousand of them copied Edmond Hall. Why do you think that the New Orleans guys had such individuality and modern young kids don't? Do you have any theory of that?
I really have never stopped... The guys...
I mean, you understand what I'm talking about.
I do, yes. I know what you're talking about.

Ten to one, they're going to sound like George Lewis. But in those days, ten to one they didn't sound like Picou. They all seemed to have their own style. Individuality seems to have dropped out of the music business.

Certainly nobody tried to play like Picou. Certainly I would never want to play like Picou. I would have maybe tried to copy a little bit with Picou, but I really never... Barry, I never tried to copy anybody.
I was going to say why not. Why didn't you try to copy anybody?
Well, it's because I had a certain feeling that I thought this should be played this way, not the way this guy sounds, not the way that guy sounds.

Practically every New Orleans clarinet player you talk to will tell you the same thing as you just said. I just wonder why, in your generation, you didn't want to sound like anybody, Barney didn't want to sound like anybody, but nowadays, like you say, every town has got its George Lewis...

Yes. It's an amazing thing. I've never been able to pinpoint why that is. I mean, my drum teacher was Cie Frazier, from the Preservation Hall Band nowadays. But I didn't want to play like him. But now the average guy, they want to play like Ram Hall or Zutty or this and that.
